rows.what: Adds a warm edge glow to skin materials, a fake subsurface warmth. It does this by text-replacing chunks of three.js's built-in toon shader at compile time, using its own varyings and its own program cache key.

rows.v2_note: Avoid: patching shader text by string. It is a silent no-op if three.js renames a chunk, and WebGPURenderer node materials have no GLSL onBeforeCompile path at all, so any rim effect must be written in TSL or the new material system. `_matSig` (shamble-core.js:356) never shares a material that has this hook, so every skin part stays its own draw call. Learn: the self-contained varyings and the program cache key were what kept the hack stable on r128.

rows.what: Precomputes, per geometry, a smoothed and mitred push direction for each vertex, so outline shells close at hard corners and keep a constant width. Results are cached by a content hash, so identical part shapes are solved once.

rows.evidence: TECHNICAL.md:47 describes the mitre capped at 2x and the 4000-entry cache cap. TECHNICAL.md:50: about 33 ms once at boot, about 1 ms per soldier (re)build, nothing per frame (measured headless).
rows.v2_note: A pure geometry algorithm with no per-frame cost. Learn: content-keyed caching made soldier rebuilds cheap. rows.what: A law-of-cosines two-bone solver: given a shoulder (or hip), a target, a pole direction and two bone lengths, it sets the upper bone's quaternion and the elbow (or knee) bend, clamping reach so the limb never locks straight. It uses preallocated scratch vectors (zero allocation) and serves both arms and legs.
rows.where: shamble-game.js:207-208 scratch vectors (_ikD, _ikDir, _ikAx, _ikUA, _ikLA, _ikQ, _ikQ2, _ikDown, _ikS, _ikT, _ikPole), 209 const ARM_L1/ARM_L2, 210-223 function solveArmIK. Calls: legs game:358, 472; arms game:415, 416, 427, 432, 435, 486, 488. The orphaned header comment is at shamble-core.js:813, directly above cabanaRepublicMap.
rows.evidence: ANIMATION_PLAN.md §6 [verified, headless]: hand on grip/rail 0.0 cm, hands during reloads 0.0 cm, leg IK stretch 0.98 (target ≤ 0.98), katana left fist to hilt 2.7 cm, CPU per soldier per frame about 51 µs for the whole animation tick.
rows.v2_note: Keep it: a small, allocation-free, well-measured solver. It is cosmetic only (ANIMATION_PLAN §1). The defaults ARM_L1 0.46 / ARM_L2 0.42 are labelled 'CHAR_MALE' but do not match the verified rig (upper arm 0.58, forearm 0.59, ANIMATION_PLAN §5). rows.system: ASCII grid map format and parser (Cabana Republic)
rows.what: Cabana Republic is drawn as a 41 x 29 ASCII grid of 10 m cells, one character per cell for road, crate, building, barracks, silo, tech point and harvest field. parseGridToMapDef turns that grid into the same map-definition object buildMap uses. Team comes from which half of the grid a cell is in, and the spawn and resupply points are placed 15 m and 7 m from the friendly barracks, toward the centre.

rows.system: Procedural canvas skins and the BK texture cache
rows.what: Ten functions each paint a 256 x 256 canvas texture (half-timber, terracotta tile, plaster, thatch, brick-and-flint, brick, slate, drystone, hedge leaves, dirt) with nearest filtering and repeat wrapping. BK.tex caches one shared copy per skin, with that skin's repeat.

Same report, PERF-2 (deferred, STATUS risks): _disposeObj3D disposes the shared BK._tex textures, so r128 re-uploads them (1 extra 256 x 256 upload per rebuild). ART_DIRECTION.md:127 and TECHNICAL.md:250: the brick-and-flint banding reads as 'candy stripes'. Code read: the legacy makers call genXTex() directly rather than BK.tex, so the 10 non-manor Cabana houses build 20 textures of their own.
rows.v2_note: Keep the technique: no external assets, painted procedurally, cached once per skin. Fix in v2: seed every painter (all of them use Math.random; the kit already has _mulberry32) so renders and A/B shots are exact. Route every caller through the cache. Never dispose cached textures on teardown. NearestFilter, the 256 px size and the palettes are look choices, so they wait for the look brief.
rows.reason: Client-side procedural builders worth keeping in shape (code technique only, appearance pending).

Code read: when the ray starts inside the capsule's cylinder, rayCapsule returns -1 (a miss), while raySphere returns 0, so a point-blank muzzle inside a torso may miss the torso. Not measured.
rows.v2_note: Keep the closed-form tests: they are small, allocation-free and easy to port. Fix the inside-start case so the capsule behaves like the sphere (a hit at t=0), and add unit tests with exact cases, which legacy never had. rows.system: Comic onomatopoeia words (gunshot and kill text pops)
rows.what: Draws words like BLAM or KO! on a canvas, caches one texture per word and colour, and pops them as pooled sprites at the muzzle (with a 150 ms cooldown) or at a kill. All the textures are pre-warmed at load.

rows.v2_note: Keep the technique: pre-baked text textures in a cache, pooled sprites, no allocation on the kill frame. It is purely cosmetic and belongs on the client, triggered by confirmed hit and kill events (LOOP_V2 §7 split feedback: hit feedback arrives when the hit is confirmed). It uses Math.random for tilt and pick, and performance.now for the cooldown. That is fine on the client, but it must never feed the simulation (STATUS.md:68 lists 11 wall-clock reads as a determinism input). The word list and colours wait for the look brief.
rows.reason: Cosmetic client FX with a proven zero-allocation pattern; the appearance waits for the look brief.

checks.corrections:
what: Pushes a circle of radius r out of every crate and wall box (barracks walls included, since they are addBox obstacles), using oriented boxes when rotated. It does the same for house colliders (oriented via their local boxes), cover boxes (skipped when standing above the top), tree squares and solid prop boxes, by the shortest axis. It is almost allocation-free: an unrotated legacy house that has no compound boxes allocates a one-element array per call (`h.boxes||[h.box]`), and Cabana has two (brickFarm at rot 0). The player, bots, the nav grid and the editor playtest all share it.
v2_note: Keep one collision function shared by players, bots and navigation, so bots and humans can never disagree. Avoid: a single sequential pass by shortest axis can jitter or leak in corners where boxes overlap. It scans every collider for every agent with no spatial index, which is O(agents × colliders) at 48+ players. Buildings, platforms and ramps rely on tickVertical's step guard rather than push-out; barracks walls are ordinary obstacles and do use push-out. Rust version: a broad-phase grid, oriented boxes and circles, and a deterministic fixed tick. Keep the ≥ 6 m gap rule (LOOP_V2 §9).

rows.system: Animation tuning table and critically damped spring
rows.what: One data object holds every animation knob: gait (duty, pelvis drop, lift, cadence bounds), spring stiffnesses, per-gun hold poses (carry / ADS / sprint), reload choreography keys, and action poses (flinch, death, draw, bayonet charge, throw, shield, katana). An analytic critically damped spring smooths every blended value and stays stable at any frame time.

Burst, auto and semi-auto fire are dispatched per frame.

rows.system: Route following, replanning and route budget
rows.what: navSteer walks a bot straight when the grid line to its goal is clear. Otherwise it follows a cached route, skipping waypoints it can see. It replans when it has no route, when the goal has moved more than 3 m, every 1.5 s, or when the bot has moved under 0.35 m in 0.8 s. At most 2 searches run per update across all bots.

rows.system: FX pool and transient combat effects
rows.what: Short-lived world effects: tracers, muzzle flashes, impact sparks by surface, shell casings, explosions, grenade blast (shock rings, dust, shrapnel, scorch, scuffs), the concussion overlay and the camera kick. Every effect is drawn from per-kind pools of meshes that are built once, and one fx[] loop fades them and returns them to the pool.

TECHNICAL:117: bot-shot FX are skipped beyond TUNE.fx.botCullR 50 m. Code read at 48ffb51 found a live bug at 1050: a `//` comment swallows the rest of the line, so pooled scuffs never get their scale, rotation or position.
rows.v2_note: Keep the pool-per-kind design with caps, and keep the fade curves as data (LOOP_V2 §7 feel kit: muzzle flash, tracer and impact per weapon). Avoid three things: the swallowed-comment bug at 1050 (scuffs show at a stale or origin transform, standing upright); the grenade flash, still a new SphereGeometry and Material per blast (1082); and fx.splice per expiry. The camera kick and concussion stay client-only and must never feed aim. The bot FX cull uses a random sequence that depends on the camera (three-teams-core report l.77), so in v2 the cull must not touch simulation randomness.
rows.reason: Cosmetic client effects. The pooling technique carries over; the look is pending.

rows.what: Keyboard and mouse listeners write a keys{} map plus mouse NDC and button flags. Hard-coded keys: WASD, Shift, Space, R, F, G, E, 1/2/3, Tab, Esc/P, the backquote key and '['. rows.what: Turns WASD into a move vector relative to the camera yaw, applies sprint (drains stamina; when it runs out, sprint locks until the bar refills to 30 %), ADS, banzai and shield speed multipliers, then smooths the velocity, clamps to the arena and resolves collision. Also drives the stamina bar.

The sim should get a world-space move direction (the client applies the camera yaw), because today's axes depend on camYaw (2751). rows.what: An isometric follow camera: a screen-space dead zone before the camera pans or looks ahead, smoothed middle-mouse yaw, ADS reaction ('pitch' flattens the view toward the crosshair, 'pan' is a Foxhole-style distance pan that keeps the player on screen), and FOV easing plus recoil, shake and a spring-damped concussion kick. Aim is cast through the stable camera base, so shake never moves the crosshair's world aim.

rows.what: All sound is generated at runtime from oscillators and noise buffers: shots per weapon, an AMK sniper report (saturated noise layers plus a convolution street echo), reload clicks, steps, clanks, impact thwacks (throttled to one per 55 ms), positional enemy shots and booms (inverse-distance gain, stereo pan against the camera's right axis), the headshot thunk, the kill tick, a looping ambient bed, and the war-room stamp and typewriter sounds. The AudioContext is created and resumed on the first pointer or key press.

rows.what: One requestAnimationFrame loop dispatches on a global mode string (menu, game, editor, charlab). Then it places the cursor, moves the sun, captures vignette shots, renders, and updates the dev overlay and the scoreboard. deploy() switches to game mode and resets the round; backToMenu() returns to the menu.
